svg.title: TOPAK E4 — Stalls that end: liveness stated for the first time, checked by TLC and not yet proved
svg.desc: The corpus's answer to failure is to stall, and every check before 2026.10.07 was of safety, under which a stall that never ends is as safe as one that ends (CR-37; ToO rev 15 §5.5). The liveness plan sorts the stalls into tiers. Two modules now extend frozen ones, so that the base's safety carries over, and add what those cannot state. Emergency_live makes ADR-0039 A2's escape hatch two invariants over ENABLED: proved (through Isabelle), certified, and proved in Lean, of the encoding. Coupling_live states that ADR-0039 §2's stall ends as four leads-to properties, under fairness conditions each named for whose obligation it is (ToO §13 A12, A18): checked by TLC, not proved. One mutation, M_HBLIVE, passes every safety check and every witness, and only a leads-to property catches it. The proofs are owed, and the four properties have the shape of the prover's first known unsound case (ADR-0046 A2). Neither module is a record: they sit under ADR-0039 (accepted, C4) and its A2 (provisional, with ADR-0052), and G11 cites them by digest.

1 · Why: a stall is safe, and so is a stall that never ends
The design's answer to failure is to stall (ToO rev 15 §5.5)

svg.text: A Thinker without a live Observer waits, a promotion without coverage waits, and a domain without an
Every check before 2026.10.07 was of safety, and a stall is safe; so is a stall that never ends.
ADR-0039 §2 makes a liveness claim in so many words: "The Thinker waits; it is not evicted. When the
Observer catches up, admits resume within the same round, or the next round is granted."

text.tspan: CR-37: no liveness property anywhere (critical review 2026.10.02)

svg.text: Every module was Init /\ [][Next]_vars with no fairness, and every property an invariant (
spec/proof-method.md §5). That is what made the proofs cheap (ToO §11.3).
Coupling across rounds, coverage at the tally, the correlator's exemption and K < R are all arguments
that a stall resolves, "and nothing checks that it does"; the model "cannot distinguish stall from deadlock".
CR-37 proposed one liveness property per coupling module under weak fairness on the heartbeat. That
is not enough, even strong (§5, SpecAnyBeat).
ToO §12 item 21: no stall is shown to end.
Not "a bad principal eventually stops", but the stalls TOPAK chooses do end, and the emergency
paths stay open while everything else is stalled.
The method stays as it is: a mutation that must break each liveness property, as with the invariants.
The plan's route: TLC's liveness checker at small constants first, then a TLAPS WF1/SF1 proof on a
decreasing measure such as seal[r] − mark[r] or seq − mark, and Lean later.

text.tspan: Why TLC's deadlock check cannot see it (Coupling_live.tla header)

svg.text: In Coupling every state has a successor: the Observer's lease, granted or ended, and the correlator
So a Thinker stalled for good is a livelock, not a deadlock: with the check on, TLC reports nothing even
under the mutation that stalls the next round for good (row d-hblive-deadlock).
Several run scripts pass -deadlock, which turns the check off altogether (the plan; §9 below).
Only a leads-to property, P ~> Q (whenever P, eventually Q), tells a stall that ends from one that does

The claim, in the plan's words

Effects need an ordered admit, so during a partition nothing commits.

text.tspan: Tier 0: "X can't block Y", invariants over ENABLED. "Prove all of these; it's cheap"

svg.text: Stated · proved · certified, before 2026.10.07: ConsultNeverCoupledAlways, LagNeverGatesAlways, DenyAlwaysAvailableAlways, in proof modules that certify
"An emergency call is admitted with no live Observer." It is the one escape hatch from the coupling stall, and it rested only on a TLC reachability witness. Its
ENABLED lemma was dropped because only Zenon proved it and Isabelle couldn't check Zenon's script (Emergency_proof.tla:401). A witness shows the call can
happen in some run; the claim needs it possible in every state where the Observer is dead.
Stated · proved · certified · proved in Lean, of the encoding: Emergency_live.tla, 32 TLC rows, two invariants proved through Isabelle; the encoding checked against TLC's graphs (§4)

text.tspan: Tier 1: real leads-to properties to model and prove, in priority order

svg.text: If the cell Observer eventually holds its lease and keeps up, every Thinker refused for its backlog is eventually admitted again, and round r+1 is eventually granted
once round r is sealed. The assumption should be A12 written as a fairness condition, so that the proof says exactly what a deployment must guarantee. "Repeat it
Stated · checked by TLC · not proved: Coupling_live.tla, four leads-to properties, 69 TLC rows (§5). The proofs are owed. The repeat for RunCoupling has no module: spec/README.md lists two
Under ADR-0024's two weak-fairness assumptions, a gated round that no seat denies eventually promotes. A proof will force a missing premise (§8).
Not stated · unmodelled. Belongs in the still-owed bootstrap Promotion module

text.tspan: 3 · Every ended lease eventually yields a seal

svg.text: Expiry, revocation and fence. A seal that never lands is a silent deadlock of the next round. Assumes consensus progress.

text.tspan: 4 · A lapsed operator is eventually re-seated by

svg.text: Lower priority: the stall is declared, and resolving it rests on people.
Each correlator's watermark eventually passes every send, so CarriedCoversSplitPath eventually applies. Useful but advisory: detection can only subtract.

text.tspan: Tier 2: declare as assumptions, don't prove

svg.text: An eventually stable leader under partial synchrony. Textbook, and the reference already tests "liveness after healing". Model it as fairness on an abstract ordering
Declared, not proved: every step Coupling_live's conditions name is one the mechanism decides and orders, so each also assumes the ordering makes progress, "which the liveness plan declares
W + L + D < T_irrev, T_obs, K: measurements, not theorems. ADR-0032 rightly defers UPPAAL; measure them with the rehearsal rig (CR-36).
Declared, not proved: T_obs and K are still placeholders (ADR-0039 §1; E2)
Weak fairness on Vote: an assumption about people, as ADR-0024 says.
Declared, not proved. Coupling_live's GrantsMade is of the same kind, "an assumption about people, declared as one", now ToO §13 A18
Lost records leave the Observer short of the seal, which shows up as a stall under A12. It doesn't need its own property.

text.tspan: What the extension relation gives, and what it adds

svg.text: Under every Mut of the base, NextL is the base's Next (NextIsNextL, proved), so the state graph is the same: 1,124 states for
Under the extension's own mutations NextL is a restriction of Next (NextLIsNext, proved under every Mut).
So SpecL => Spec is proved (SpecLImpliesSpec), and every invariant the base's proof module proves holds of SpecL, each under
the hypothesis it has there: the safety carries over.
Fairness is conjoined, as SpecA12 == SpecL /\ A12, so a theorem about SpecL holds of every fair spec the module defines.
The base is never edited. The plan had said "a successor module, as Lease_A1 did"; the modules extend instead, as a proof module
Frozen from G11 on: the two modules, their proof modules and their results files (G11 §3).

text.tspan: 4 · Tier 0: the escape hatch is a property, not only a witness:

svg.text: A2: "a person seated by the break-glass roster's quorum for one round does not wait on an Observer." Emergency.tla showed this as a behaviour, its
witness w3. The claim is that once the seat is live, nothing the Observer does can stop its calls, in any state.
EmergencyNeverCoupled == \A t \in Tools : (em.live /\ t \in em.envelope) => ENABLED EmAdmit(t): "while the seat is live, a call of any
tool in its envelope can be admitted, whatever the Observer's state".
EmergencyCallsWithoutObserver == (em.live /\ ~obsLive) => \E t \in Tools : ENABLED EmAdmit(t): "while the seat is live and the
Observer is not, some emergency call can be admitted". The envelope is never empty: it holds te (ADR-0052 R1) and, in this model, t1 (EnvelopeHasT1,
To ask ENABLED of the admit, EmCall is split into its two outcomes, EmAdmit and EmRefuse; under every Mut of Emergency.tla the two together are
EmCall exactly, so the state graph is the same.
Scope: the calls of a live seat, not the seating. "An activation that waited for a live Observer would pass every check here."
M_EMCOUPLE: R3 extended to the emergency seat. M_EMCOUPLE2: the same from the seat's second round on; every invariant holds and w3 is still reached,
in round one, so only the two properties catch it.
M_EMCOUPLE: R3 extended to the emergency seat
M_EMCOUPLE2: coupled from the seat's second round on

TLC checks (Emergency_live-results-2026.10.07.txt): Rows: 32 · as expected: 32 · not as expected: none. Emergency's seven mutations each leave both properties holding on that mutation's own state graph: none of them couples the emergency seat. — : no row of this file.
For every round bound: EmergencyNeverCoupledAlways and EmergencyCallsWithoutObserverAlways under Mut
\notin {"M_EMCOUPLE", "M_EMCOUPLE2"}; SpecLImpliesSpec under every Mut, and with it Emergency_proof's six for
EmergencyNeverCoupled holds in every state under its hypothesis, reachable or not: the admit's guard does not read the
Observer. EmergencyCallsWithoutObserver needs one fact of the reachable states, EnvelopeHasTe, inductive under
Certified (Emergency_live-proof-cert-results-2026.10.07.txt): 160 obligations: 97 trivial, closed by tlapm; 56 SMT, each proof
accepted by ethos; 0 Zenon; 2 Isabelle; 5 LS4, which no checker confirms.
Why Isabelle. The dropped lemma failed on the record the admit writes to calls': cvc5 could not eliminate calls' =
{...}, and Zenon's script left the equality of two records unproved, which Isabelle refuses. Here Isabelle proves each
property in one step from its expansion (ExpandENABLED, Isa).
Why one step each. Under a binder, tlapm 7824dab hands an unexpanded ENABLED to its backends as a constant that does
not depend on the bound variable: it proves (\E t \in Tools : ENABLED EmAdmit(t)) => (\A t \in Tools :
ENABLED EmAdmit(t)), which is false, and ethos accepts cvc5's proof. Found writing this module (G11 §3 result 1;

text.tspan: · proved in Lean, of the encoding

svg.text: Emergency.tla and Emergency_live.tla re-encoded in one file as a transition system. ENABLED A is Enabled A (
Temporal.lean): a successor in the encoding's State type; EmAdmit fixes each primed variable to a value of its type, so the
EmergencyNeverCoupledValid: under every other Mut, in every state, reachable or not.
EmergencyNeverCoupledAlways, EmergencyCallsWithoutObserverAlways: in every state Spec reaches, and so every
state SpecL reaches, under NoCoupledRound, that no round in which the seat can be live is coupled. The weakest
hypothesis there is: the two …Iff theorems prove each property holds exactly when it does.
UnobservedEmergencyCallEnabledAlways, in place of the lemma Emergency_proof dropped: stated of the frozen
module's own Next, for every Mut and every MaxRound.
Induction on reachable states, in place of LS4; kernel-checked and replayed (TopakSpec-results-2026.10.07.txt,
d365231c3ae3dd61). A theorem of the encoding, not of the frozen text; its fidelity is read, and here also checked (right).
The encoding checked against TLC's state graphs (ADR-0053 R6; GraphCheckEmergency-results-2026.10.07.txt, a18bf90ba38eca61). A MATCH: no edge that is not a step of the relation,
no step that is not an edge or a stutter, the same initial states, and every property TLC's value in every state, the two over ENABLED included (— for Emergency, which does not state them). At
Under the two coupling mutations the two properties are false in the same states in TLC's graph and in the encoding. The mirror's theorems are proved; this run evaluates them on the graphs, a test.

ADR-0046 A2: "Two of the four leads-to properties Coupling_live.tla states are quantified and all four have ENABLED premises." The two admit properties also need K ≥ 1; the two grant properties hold at K = 0 as well (the module's header).

text.tspan: What it says, and whose obligation it is

svg.text: An Observer without a lease is granted its next round. The first grant is the mechanism's, on its seating's tally; every
later one is an operator's successor grant, made with a live lease and a live peer (ADR-0031 A3; ADR-0050 §2, §4).

text.tspan: In part an assumption about operators.

svg.text: KeepUp: the heartbeat that reports a watermark within K of the Thinker's sequence while its round is live (§1, condition
3), and the seal once it has ended (§2, coverage): in some tenure, the Observer keeps up. A lease is granted for one
round (ADR-0031 §2), so an Observer is without a lease between its rounds and its heartbeats stop there (ADR-0039
Strong, because its lease may end first, so KeepUp is
enabled only intermittently and weak fairness on it is not
every heartbeat that keeps up"), SpecAnyBeat: broken
The Thinker keeps asking, and not only while its Observer is stale or without a lease. Met jointly: by the Thinker's
asking, by heartbeats within T_obs, and by how the operators lay out the Observer's rounds against the Thinker's
(finding 3). Rounds that overlap need two cell Observers, since a principal holds one lease at a time.
Strong, because Stale or EndO may follow every heartbeat
that keeps up, so Admit is enabled only intermittently
A grant that can be made is made. The Thinker asks for none: its first round is granted by the mechanism when its
seating's tally completes, and every later round by an operator with a live lease and a live peer. An assumption
The ordering makes progress. Every step these conditions name is one the mechanism decides and orders

A12 (ToO rev 15 §13): "Every Run Thinker's cell Observer keeps up: heartbeats within T_obs, watermark within K, coverage to each seal". If it fails, nothing is lost to safety: the Thinker's admits and its next round stall, and a deployment that will not accept the stall declares D-0039-1. A18, new in revision 15: "A refused

Thinker asks again, and grants are made". If it fails, the coupling stall may never end, and the leads-to properties that say it ends are void. G11 item 105 had found that §13 did not yet list these two.

text.tspan: What the module did not assume, and why (its header; the plan)

svg.text: "The lease is eventually held for good" would be simpler, "and no one-Observer cell meets it": its lease is for one round.
Fairness on any heartbeat, which CR-37 proposed weak, "is not enough even strong: a heartbeat that repeats an old watermark keeps the
Observer fresh and never covers the backlog" (SpecAnyBeat).
Weak fairness on KeepUp or on Admit (SpecWFKeepUp, SpecWFAdmit): each action is enabled only intermittently, and each row breaks its
Stale restricted to "no heartbeat since": the plan offered it beside strong fairness on Admit. The module takes strong fairness, as
ThinkerAsks; Stale is Coupling.tla's, which is frozen.
Fairness only on actions of NextL, "so no choice of them can leave a spec with no behaviour"; the NoBehaviour rows check it of each fair
spec under which a row holds.

Witnesses: Coupling's four, NeverRoundTwo, NeverRefused, NeverStaleRefusal and NeverBacklogRefusal, and the module's three: NeverRoundTwoAfterReading (a round that admitted something, read to its seal and followed), NeverBacklogRefusalStep (a refusal for the backlog, as a step) and NeverAdmitted. "Has a behaviour": NoBehaviour == <>FALSE is violated, so the fair spec is not vacuous. One worker and a fixed fingerprint function, so a liveness
counterexample is the same on every run (spec/README.md).

text.tspan: What TLC's rows are evidence of

svg.text: Checked: Rows: 69 · as expected: 69 · not as expected: none (Coupling_live-results-2026.10.07.txt).
At small constants only: K=1, R=3, MaxRound=2 (1,124 states) and K=2, R=4, MaxRound=3 (11,908); one Thinker, its cell Observer and one correlator.
"A leads-to property checked by TLC is checked at small constants" (G11 §3, "What these checks are").
Each fairness condition is dropped or weakened in a row that must break, and each mutation that must break a property has a row that does: the method of the invariants, kept.

text.tspan: : the safety is proved, the liveness is not

svg.text: Proved, for every K, R and MaxRound in Nat: SpecLImpliesSpec == SpecL => Spec under every Mut; NoAdmitWithoutLiveObserverAlwaysL, UnreadBoundedAlwaysL, CorrelatorNeverGatesAlwaysL, each under
the hypothesis it has in Coupling_proof; SafeAlwaysL under none, M_HBLIVE, M_HBCOUPLED.
Certified (Coupling_live-proof-cert-results-2026.10.08.txt): 31 obligations: 17 trivial, 12 SMT accepted by ethos, 2 LS4, which no checker confirms.
Nothing in it uses fairness: a theorem about SpecL holds of every fair spec, since each adds conjuncts to it.
Not proved: the four leads-to properties. They are owed, with K ≥ 1 a hypothesis of the two admit properties (G11 §7 item 105; §8: "No liveness is proved").

text.tspan: : every safety check and every witness pass, and only a leads-to property catches it (G11 §3 result 8; ToO §5.5, §11.3)

svg.text: The mutation (Coupling_live.tla): HeartbeatL(r, w) adds Mut # "M_HBLIVE" \/ tLive to Heartbeat, so an Observer may heartbeat only while its Thinker's lease is live. The trace is TLC's counterexample to GrantStallEnds under SpecFull, every fairness condition on (row m-hblive-grant, Coupling_live-results-2026.10.07.txt), read at build time: 9 states, then back to state 8 by GrantO, for ever. Shown: the variables that move.
GrantO: back to state 8, for ever
States 1–6: round 1 is granted, the Observer leased, the Thinker refused (the Observer stale), the Observer heartbeats at watermark 0, and one
State 7: EndRoundT seals round 1 at 1. The round ends unread.
States 8–9: tLive = FALSE, so under M_HBLIVE no heartbeat is enabled and mark[1] stays 0 below seal[1] = 1: never read. GrantT asks
mark[round] >= seal[round] (Coupling.tla §2) and is never enabled: round 2 is never granted.
The Observer's lease toggles, EndO and GrantO, so every state has a successor. Unmutated, the same prefix ends: row l-none-grant holds.

text.tspan: What every other check sees under

svg.text: Safe holds, on all of Coupling's 1,124 states: "no invariant over the variables can tell M_HBLIVE from none" (the rows file).
Every witness is reached, NeverRoundTwoAfterReading among them: some behaviours read round 1 to its seal before it ends.
TLC's deadlock check, on: no terminal state (d-hblive-deadlock).
AdmitStallEnds and AdmitsResume hold. GrantStallEnds and NextRoundGranted break, also at K=2, R=4, MaxRound=3.
Coupling_live_proof proves SafeAlwaysL under M_HBLIVE: the safety theorems are true of it.

Its twin, M_HBCOUPLED, is caught twice: it breaks AdmitStallEnds, and it admits nothing, so Coupling's own witness run catches it too (

text.tspan: 7 · Why the proof is owed, and why it is hard (ADR-0046 A2; Coupling_live_proof.tla's header; ToO §5.5)
What a proof of a leads-to needs

svg.text: A WF1 or SF1 step on a decreasing measure, such as seal[r] − mark[r] or seq − mark (the plan's
That step needs a quantified leads-to hypothesis inside the proof, which PTL cannot combine from
spec/README.md: "A liveness property also needs a variant and a WF1-shaped proof; for

text.tspan: The prover's two known unsound cases (T-0045-31; Batch 37)

svg.text: First: a term under a binder. tlapm 7824dab hands SMT, Zenon and Isabelle an untranslated term, an
unexpanded ENABLED or \cdot or a temporal formula, as an opaque constant that does not depend on
any variable bound around it, so a false statement can prove and certify.
Among those that certify: a universal temporal statement from a true one-instance lemma, and Spec =>
[]P for a quantified P from a true Spec => []P'. No check detects this case (G11 item 104).
Second: two terms with one name, by a 20-bit hash tlapm does not check; FALSE proves and certifies
No result in the 24 proof modules rests on either (proof-scan-results-2026.10.08.txt).

text.tspan: The four have the first case's shape

svg.text: Two of the four are quantified: AdmitsResume over n, NextRoundGranted over r.
All four have ENABLED premises (ADR-0046 A2).
So a TLAPS proof would put the very terms the first case drops a bound variable from under the binders a
In TLAPS, no route for a measure step under the rule is known yet.

text.tspan: The rule, and the other route

svg.text: The rule (spec/proof-certification.md §10): in a step SMT, Zenon or Isabelle discharges, no
untranslated term may mention a variable bound in the obligation. A temporal property of a parameter is a
hidden definition, LT(n) == ..., expanded only in a PTL step; an ENABLED goal is proved by expanding it
Emergency_live_proof is written so: each ENABLED goal is expanded in the one step that proves it.
Lean (ADR-0053): "A proof of them in Lean cannot meet either case." The plan put Lean later, because
its packages would first need a model of infinite behaviours and fairness.

text.tspan: 8 · What is not stated: Tier 1 items 2–5, each unmodelled (ToO rev 15 §5.5; G11 §7 item 105)
2 · The Build promotion stall resolves (ADR-0024 §2, A2.3)
Open · not stated · a premise missing

svg.text: Under the two weak-fairness assumptions ADR-0024 already states, on Vote and on the Observer's
lease and coverage, a gated round that no seat denies eventually promotes.
The missing premise: the rules epoch eventually stops changing. Every epoch change voids votes in
flight, so repeated fences can starve a promotion forever. A proof will force it, and the corpus does not
Belongs in the still-owed bootstrap Promotion module.
The reference's e2e shows one stalled promotion completed by a heartbeat (CR-37): a run, not a

text.tspan: 3 · Every ended lease eventually yields a seal

svg.text: Expiry (I15, proposed as EndRound(Expired) and ordered), revocation and fence.
The grant guard reads seal[r], so a seal that never lands is a silent deadlock of the next round.

text.tspan: 4 · A lapsed operator is eventually re-seated by a quorum

svg.text: ADR-0050 (provisional): a domain without an operator waits.
Lower priority: the stall is declared, and resolving it rests on people.
Under fairness on the correlator's fold, each correlator's watermark eventually passes every send, so
Useful but advisory, since detection can only subtract.
Every run script listed passes -deadlock, which turns off TLC's report of a state with no successor. Each line is one module at one set of
constants, unmutated, through a wrapper that EXTENDS it and adds only definitions, so the state graph is the module's own.
TLC checks NotTerminal (Terminal == ~ENABLED of the next-state relation) and, where that is violated, TerminalAtBound: every terminal
